newsitem.title: USA: N.J. man indicted for helping brother flee arrest.
newsitem.headline: N.J. man indicted for helping brother flee arrest.

text.p: A New Jersey man was arraigned on Wednesday in the plot to blow up New York City landmarks for allegedly driving his brother to the airport, knowing that he had participated in the World trade Centre bombing days earlier, officials said.
Mohammed Abouhalima pleaded not guilty before U.S. District Court Judge Michael Mukasey. The judge ruled he would stay in jail until a bail hearing next Tuesday.

Abouhalima had previously been indicted in August, 1993, on the broader charge of seditious conspiracy for the same driving act and on charges of participating in the plot to kill Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak., U.S. Attorney's Office spokesman Marvin Smilon said.

Prosecutors agreed to sever his case from those of his co-defendants. Smilon said the government had previously decided not to pursue the Mubarak charge and now, because of this superceding indictment, the government would also not pursue the seditious conspiracy charge.
The indictment was handed up in mid-July and unsealed on Wednesday, Smilon said.
Abouhalima, 32, a cabdriver, was arrested on Wednesday morning outside his home in Avenel, N.J., Smilon said. If convicted, he could face 15 years in prison.

According to the indictment, Abouhalima drove his brother, Mahmud Abouhalima, to John F. Kennedy International Airport in late February or early March of 1993 so that he would not be arrested in connection with the Feb. 26, 1993 bombing.

Mahmud Abouhalima was arrested on March 10, 1993, in his native Egypt. He was convicted in March, 1994, of planting a bomb at the World Trade Centre that killed six people and injured more than 1,000.

Mahmud Abouhalima was an unindicted co-conspirator in the plot to blow up New York City landmarks. Mohammed Abouhalima's current charge stems from that case, in which 10 people were convicted, including radical Egyptian cleric Sheikh Abdel-Rahman.
